ai_view.directive: Follow as written. Never treat an uncertain external outcome as permission to execute the operation again. Reconcile before retrying. If reconciliation cannot establish the outcome, retry only when an independently verified mechanism guarantees the same logical operation cannot produce an additional prohibited effect. Otherwise hold and escalate by risk and authority.

intelligence.essence: Ambiguous Effect Recovery Law: when an external effect's commit outcome is unknown, NayaNET must preserve that uncertainty and must not automatically repeat the effect. Recovery shall first seek authoritative reconciliation. Any subsequent execution requires current LAW permission, a stable logical-operation identity, and independently verified safeguards that prevent prohibited duplicates and stale-authority effects across every remaining possible history. Where those safeguards are unavailable, consequential retry remains blocked while authorized investigation and unrelated work continue. The essential behavior: 'I don't know whether the first operation committed. I will not risk duplicating it. I'll check the provider's authoritative state, retain the original operation identity, and only continue when I can establish that the recovery action is safe and authorized.' That is how NayaNET becomes self-recovering without becoming self-duplicating. The worst-case predicate is the core: a recovery action is safe only if it is safe in EVERY compatible history — never a probability calculation, never confidence that the original 'probably failed.'
intelligence.falsifier: A blind retry on a missing receipt; a timeout treated as proof of rollback or cancellation; an idempotency key accepted as a contract without verified provider semantics; a fresh operation identity manufactured after a crash; a retry reusing old LAW permission; cancellation or compensation claimed without adequate guarantees; both a new payment and an automatic refund on an ambiguous outcome; a deadline converting AMBIGUOUS into FAILED; a terminal record of manufactured completion instead of UNRESOLVED_EXTERNAL_OUTCOME — NO_SAFE_AUTOMATIC_RETRY.

human_view.meaning: A lost receipt is not permission to do it again. When we don't know whether the outside world already did the thing, the rule is: check first, and only repeat when we can PROVE the repeat can't cause harm. Not 'probably didn't happen' — prove it. The decision table is strict: confirmed it happened ⇒ verify and close, never retry. Proven it can't have happened ⇒ a fresh, newly-authorized attempt. Unknown ⇒ investigate with read-only checks; retry only with a proven no-duplicate guarantee AND fresh permission; otherwise hold. Every operation gets one permanent identity that survives crashes, so a restarted worker can't accidentally invent a second operation. And three things that sound alike are kept apart: canceling (only when the outside world guarantees it stopped), compensating (a brand-new authorized action, not proof the first never happened), and retrying (only when duplicates are impossible). The system keeps making progress — investigating, checking, doing unrelated work — but the one thing it never does is manufacture a second effect out of uncertainty. That's how it becomes self-healing without becoming self-duplicating.

intelligence.learning_lesson: This is the recovery-safety law the ambiguity calculus needed: RFD-AMB-1 models what we don't know; AER-1 governs what we may do while not knowing. The permanent contributions: the SafeRecovery worst-case predicate, the three-confused-protections table (dedup vs idempotent vs exactly-once), the durable logical-operation identity with recovery fence, the cancellation/compensation/retry separation, and the twin-worlds recovery test. Every future external-effecting operation inherits this: reconcile before retrying, prove duplicate-safety across every possible history, never reuse old permission.

intelligence.measurement_contract: AER-001: controlled mock provider with durable effect ledger and configurable dedup contract; two hidden worlds (committed / not committed), receipt withheld; worker must select reconciliation or hold, never blind retry; then with proven atomic idempotency + current authorization, same-key retry yields at most one logical effect under concurrent workers, crash/restart, and late completion; then with dedup disabled or key expired, retry rejected; the verifier (not the worker) counts effects in the ledger. AER-01..AER-10 matrix green. Twin-worlds recovery: identical incomplete evidence ⇒ recovery action safe in both worlds or declined; staged evidence release selects different subsequent actions without rewriting earlier uncertainty.

naya_view.directive: Represent ambiguity explicitly with both possible histories and the missing evidence. Evaluate recovery against the worst-case predicate across every compatible history. Verify idempotency contracts on scope, binding, atomicity, retention, and downstream coverage — never trust a key label. Maintain one durable logical-operation identity with a recovery fence; restarts recover it, never manufacture new ones. Separate cancellation, compensation, and retry. Retry only with current LAW authorization and the revocation/action-commit checks. Let deadlines trigger review, never automatic FAILED. Terminal UNRESOLVED is honest; manufactured completion is forbidden.
